items.title: Network-guided identification of candidate biomarkers for COPD-associated comorbidities using deep learning and real-world transcriptomic data
items.abstract_or_text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexists with infections, metabolic disease, cardiovascular disease, inflammatory lung injury and lung cancer. Molecular markers derived by comparing a comorbidity with healthy controls need not identify the transition from an established COPD state to that comorbidity. We therefore developed a two-stage computational strategy that asks a narrower question: which proteins can distinguish COPD samples from samples annotated with a specific COPD-associated comorbidity? First, a Human Protein Network (HPN; 17,302 proteins and 492,195 relationships) was encoded by 20 graph-derived features. A convolutional-neural-network ensemble, termed the functional-distance model (FDM), was trained on known drug-target-indication relationships. Stored training-set predictions yielded an apparent balanced accuracy of 0.811 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.627; these values describe resubstitution performance and are not an independent estimate of generalization. The COPD-centred network search evaluated 2,645 nearby proteins and retained 224 candidates using a COPD FDM score above 0.50. Candidate expression was then tested in independently assembled public patient-derived transcriptomic data using simple one-feature classifiers and cross-validation. The resulting exploratory panel contained GTF2I for bacterial infection, UBXN7 for type 2 diabetes, LIFR for hypertension, SRGN for lung neoplasm and FGF4 for pneumonitis. Across the saved cross-validation predictions, balanced accuracy ranged from 0.838 to 0.970 and MCC from 0.726 to 0.941. SRGN has direct experimental support in non-small-cell lung cancer, whereas the remaining candidates have varying indirect mechanistic support and should be regarded as hypotheses rather than established disease biomarkers. This work demonstrates an orthogonal discovery framework in which network-based functional prioritization and patient-derived molecular discrimination constrain one another. Its main contribution is methodological: it provides a reusable strategy for generating comorbidity-specific biomarker hypotheses from an index-disease state. Prospective longitudinal cohorts are required before claims of progression prediction or clinical utility can be made.

items.title: flashscenic: Accelerated GRN Analysis with RegDiffusion for Large-Scale Single-Cell Data
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis via the SCENIC framework provides biologically interpretable cell-state representations through motif-validated transcription factor (TF) regulon activities. However, sequential, CPU-bound implementations (pySCENIC) constrain scalability to highly variable genes and make the repeated executions needed to resolve network stochasticity computationally prohibitive. Furthermore, while regulon activity is hypothesized to mitigate technical batch effects, its integration performance has never been quantitatively assessed against modern data integration benchmarks. We present flashscenic, an end-to-end GPU-accelerated framework that resolves these bottlenecks and expands the practical scope of single-cell regulatory genomics. By reformulating module construction, cisTarget motif pruning, and AUCell scoring into batched GPU tensor operations, flashscenic achieves a 12- to 27-fold downstream speedup over pySCENIC, while maintaining strict numerical equivalence (Pearson r = 0.9996). Leveraging this throughput, we conducted the first systematic benchmark of nine consensus aggregation strategies across multiple independent tissue cohorts, demonstrating that discrete post-pruning recurrence voting ([≥]50% recurrence, [≥]5 targets per regulon) maximizes biological fidelity. Finally, data integration benchmarking across a 116,043-cell acute myeloid leukemia (AML) atlas quantitatively demonstrates that uncorrected TF activity provides an intrinsic, unsupervised batch-integration benefit over raw PCA. Combining it with a standard batch integration method matches or outperforms canonical expression-based integration while accurately recovering lineage-defining and oncogenic regulators (CEBPA, HOXA9). flashscenic is available via pip install flashscenic, with source code and tutorials at https://github.com/haozhu233/flashscenic.

items.title: An Agentic AI Pipeline for an Evidence-Grounded Environmental Health Public Information System: Development and Evaluation
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Existing environmental and health information systems typically provide isolated data streams, requiring users to interpret heterogeneous information sources without personalized guidance. Residents and health providers of urban regions with complex environmental conditions, such as the Salt Lake Valley, frequently seek timely, location-specific information about weather, air quality, and their associated health impacts, but may find it difficult to integrate this information in their decision-making, precluding the effective translation of valuable environmental health information into action. Objective: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that delivers evidence-grounded, neighborhood-scale responses to health-related environmental questions raised lay persons by dynamically orchestrating authoritative weather, neighborhood-scale environmental observations, air quality, and health-evidence resources. Methods: We developed an agentic AI pipeline using LangGraph and OpenAI large language models to interpret natural language queries, select and invoke relevant external tools, retrieve real-time environmental data and evidence-based health guidance, and synthesize responses. The pipeline integrates multiple authoritative resources, including weather forecasts, air-quality observations, geospatial services, and a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module built from asthma-related clinical guidance. The system incorporates fallback mechanisms to improve robustness when external services are unavailable. We evaluated the pipeline using a curated benchmark of representative user questions, assessing tool-needed recognition, correct tool selection, avoidance of irrelevant tools, parameter mapping, analytic pathway selection, and incorporation of tool outputs into the final response. Results: The developed system successfully integrated heterogeneous environmental and health information sources into a unified conversational interface that produces evidence-grounded, neighborhood-scale responses for the Salt Lake Valley. Evaluation demonstrated generally strong tool recognition, parameter mapping, and incorporation of retrieved information across diverse question types, supporting the pipeline's ability to retrieve and integrate authoritative environmental and health information consumable by lay persons and providing an important step for the T3 and T4 phases of the translational pipeline of exposure health informatics. Conclusions: By combining existing environmental health knowledge with local sensor observations and neighborhood-scale environmental measurements, and authoritative state and national weather and air quality resources, the system delivers more localized and context-aware guidance than approaches that rely on authoritative regional or state-level information. Rather than depending on the internal knowledge of a large language model, the pipeline dynamically retrieves, synthesizes, and attributes evidence from authoritative sources. The modular architecture enables seamless integration of additional environmental data streams, health knowledge sources, and geographic regions, providing a scalable foundation for future translational pipelines, completing the T3 to T4 path for environmental health.

items.title: GlioMIL: A Frozen-Backbone Multiple-Instance Learning Framework for Calibrated and Explainable Glioma Radiogenomics
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Non-invasive prediction of glioma molecular status from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) could reduce reliance on invasive biopsy. Still, deep-learning pipelines for this task are often trained on small cohorts and rarely assessed for calibration or explainability. We present GlioMIL, a 2.5D multiple-instance-learning (MIL) framework predicting isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status, tumour grade, O 6 -methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation, and 1p/19q codeletion from multi-contrast MRI, representing each tumour as a bag of tumour-guided axial slices embedded by a frozen, ImageNet-pretrained backbone and aggregated via attention-based pooling feeding multi-task heads. On a publicly available glioma cohort, a controlled five-way ablation with bootstrap confidence intervals and paired significance testing shows this frozen-backbone approach matches a fully-supervised 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) baseline, and that fusing standardised clinical and radiomic features into the pooled representation significantly improves over image-only multi-task learning for IDH and grade. However, a plain classifier on clinical and radiomic features alone, with no image input, matches or significantly exceeds the fused model on these tasks, so the frozen image branch adds no predictive value beyond structured features. MGMT and 1p/19q codeletion remain close to chance across all conditions. The fusion model is label-efficient and reasonably well calibrated, but its attention weights correspond to tumour regions only at a near-chance level, cautioning against treating attention as a reliable spatial explanation. We report our evaluation protocol, including rejection of an earlier flawed ensembling scheme and a per-fold feature-normalisation correction, to support trustworthy, reproducible reporting.

items.title: Predicting Pathway Dependency in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma from Hallmark Transcriptomic Features
items.abstract_or_text: Despite frequent pathway activation, targeted molecular therapy remains limited in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), highlighting the need to distinguish activation from dependence. Dependency is functional, context-specific, and coupled; mutations or expression alone cannot establish it. No validated framework identifies tumor pathway dependencies from baseline molecular profiles. We developed a transcriptome-based framework to infer pathway dependency in HNSCC. Nine Elastic Net models used 50 MSigDB Hallmark activity profiles from 953 GDSC cell lines and drug responses pooled across compounds annotated to each pathway. Cross-validated R2 ranged from 0.17 (IGF1R) to 0.48 (P53); leave-one-pathway-out validation retained rank agreement (Spearman {rho} = 0.19-0.56) for pathways with no drug response observed during training. We validated the models using pharmacological, genomic, and proteomic data, then applied them to TCGA-HNSC (n = 565) and GSE65858 (n = 256), examining HPV status, age, stage, tobacco history, and CD8+ infiltration. Seven of nine pathways were higher in HPV+ tumors and replicated directionally in GSE65858. Among TP53-wild-type tumors, HPV remained linked to greater P53 dependency ({beta} = +0.37, q = 0.010); HPV+ tumors also had higher p53 transcriptional activity, suggesting residual p53 function despite E6 expression. The codependency signature had a dominant global axis (PC1 = 62.3% variance; Cronbach's = 0.91), replicated across cohorts (Tucker congruence = 0.996), but largely reflected CD8+ T-cell infiltration ({rho} = 0.80). The framework uses RNA-sequenced bulk tumor cohorts to assess baseline transcriptome-based dependencies and match pathway-directed agents to likely responders before treatment. It is not prognostic.

items.title: Integrative systems biology identifies shared neuroimmune co-expression programmes across pulmonary tuberculosis and Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background : There is growing evidence that pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) exerts long-lasting systemic effects on brain function, whereas Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic neuroimmune disorder. BCG vaccination studies suggest that tuberculosis-associated immune pathways influence AD-related biology. However, whether PTB-associated co-expression programmes exhibit concordant activity in AD and display reproducible neuroanatomical organization within the human brain remains unknown. We hypothesized that PTB-associated co-expression programmes would exhibit concordant transcriptional activity in AD, retain aspects of their underlying co-expression architecture across diseases, and identify shared neuroimmune mechanisms relevant to chronic infection and neurodegeneration. We implemented an integrative systems biology framework combining whole-blood transcriptomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, functional enrichment, immune-cell deconvolution, and machine learning to identify PTB-associated co-expression programmes and prioritize biomarkers. These programmes were validated in two independent PTB cohorts, evaluated in an AD dataset, and mapped onto the Allen Human Brain Atlas to characterize neuroanatomical organization. Results: Active PTB was associated with widespread transcriptional remodeling, with 1,389 dysregulated genes organized into 16 PTB-associated co-expression modules. Nested machine learning identified a 12-gene biomarker signature that demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in the discovery cohort (AUC ≈ 0.99) and retained performance in two independent external PTB datasets without model retraining. Majority of PTB-derived immune co-expression modules exhibited concordant activity in the independent AD cohort. Formal module-preservation analysis demonstrated that several PTB-derived networks retained moderate preservation in AD, supporting partial conservation of co-expression architecture across diseases. Brain transcriptomic mapping demonstrated reproducible region-specific organization across adult brain donors. Integrated neuroanatomical contextualization prioritized a subset of PTB-derived neuroimmune modules using cross-disease transcriptional activity, regional specificity, and inter-donor reproducibility, revealing neuroimmune transcriptional programmes shared across infection and neurodegeneration. Conclusions: Our findings establish a systems-level framework for investigating shared neuroimmune processes across chronic infection and neurodegeneration while identifying reproducible co-expression modules and candidate biomarkers for future studies.

items.title: Autonomous Hypothesis Testing Against Public Biomedical Data with Literature-Grounded Calibration
items.abstract_or_text: Public biomedical repositories contain petabytes of data, yet testing hypotheses against those resources still requires expert effort. I present a four-phase blinded workflow for autonomous computational hypothesis testing: an agent receives a natural-language hypothesis, discovers public datasets with academic publisher domains blocked, executes an analysis pipeline and validates findings against the literature. Published studies serve as calibration rulers, measuring how closely an autonomous workflow approaches known answers before it is trusted on unknown ones. Across five biomedical tasks spanning bacterial genomics, single-cell multiomics, metagenomics, cancer genomics and GWAS functional genomics, the agent scored 5–9 out of 10 on pre-specified rubrics in 20–188 minutes (the single-cell multiomics score was corrected from an initial 8 to 5 after blinded judge review identified over-credited criteria; see Methods). An exploratory comparison across three successive model generations found scores directionally higher for the first generation (claude-opus-4-6) on all five tasks (one-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.031, rank-biserial r = 1.0; n = 5 studies), with newer models completing tasks faster; the benchmark also exposed generation-specific safety policy and schema differences that silently confound cross-generation comparisons if not corrected. Failures fell into three categories, tool-version sensitivity, data-scope limitation and analytical completeness, all self-diagnosed by the validation phase in all five cases examined here without human prompting. These results introduce a calibration framework and failure taxonomy for characterising when autonomous computational science workflows should and should not be trusted.

items.title: Neural shape models enable cohort-scale simulation of knee cartilage mechanics
items.abstract_or_text: Knee osteoarthritis affects over 350 million people worldwide, is a leading cause of disability, and carries substantial costs. Cartilage mechanical load is believed to play a critical role in osteoarthritis pathophysiology, yet clinical biomechanics research uses external measures of joint loading that do not capture tissue-level load. We developed a fully-automated pipeline that builds biomechanical knee models from a single MRI using deep learning-based segmentation and neural shape models, and elastic foundation contact to simulate gait. Applied to 756 knees from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, each simulated under the same 10 standardized gaits, the pipeline converged in 99.6% of 7,560 simulations. Medial tibial pressure decreased from healthy to incident to mild osteoarthritis as disease-related shape changes enlarged contact area, an effect reproduced in simulations of synthetic knees. Yet within knees, medial cartilage thinned fastest over six years in regions of highest pressure, with stronger relationships in incident and mild osteoarthritis knees. Automated simulations provided cohort-scale, tissue-level support for mechanical theories of osteoarthritis progression and a framework for prospectively quantifying cartilage load to guide mechanical interventions.

items.title: The Bench-to-Bedside Journey of Deep Learning in Dermato-Oncology: A Systematic Review of Clinical Readiness Across the Translational Continuum
items.abstract_or_text: Deep learning systems have matched dermatologists on curated skin cancer image sets for almost a decade, but evidence from patient care has accumulated slowly and unevenly. This systematic review mapped where that evidence now sits along the translational continuum. A reproducible PubMed search run in August 2026 identified 656 records; after single-screener selection against pre-specified criteria and full-text assessment of 39 reports, 29 clinical-stage studies (prospective, controlled, or real-world evaluations of AI for cutaneous malignancy in patients) were included and staged as prospective standalone accuracy (n = 19), prospective clinician-with-AI use (n = 5), controlled evaluation (n = 1), or real-world deployment (n = 4). Risk of bias, appraised with QUADAS-2, ROBINS-I, or JBI tools, was high or serious in 24 studies, most often because of partial verification and preselected lesion spectra, and the certainty of every principal finding was low or very low (GRADE). No included study was a randomised trial with patient outcomes, and none reported stage at diagnosis, mortality, or overdiagnosis. Across modalities, sensitivity held up in prospective use, commonly above 90% at the pre-set operating point, while specificity fell to between 9% and 85% and was frequently lower than that of the clinicians it was compared against. Performance moved with acquisition hardware, lesion spectrum, and skin type, and one market-approved dermoscopic classifier reached areas under the curve of 0.54 to 0.62 in two Australian primary care studies. One product family progressed from prospective accuracy to national-pathway deployment under a conditional health technology recommendation, with human second reading overturning a large share of automated discharges. We argue that the reported specificity loss reflects safety-first operating points, spectrum preselection, and the choice of comparator rather than model failure alone, and propose readiness criteria linking each translational stage to the evidence needed before autonomous or primary-care use. The review followed PRISMA 2020, was not registered, and received no external funding.

items.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney
items.abstract_or_text: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from human kidney tissue. Kidzoi accurately predicts cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility and improves regulatory variant effect prediction in proximal tubule cells by up to 23% in terms of AUROC over existing models. Furthermore, Kidzoi effectively prioritizes genome-wide association study (GWAS) fine-mapped causal variants associated with kidney function (estimated glomerular filtration rate based on both creatinine and cystatin C; eGFRcr-cys) while resolving their cell-type specificity. Systematic ablation of flanking sequence indicates that a local context of 32-64kbp, representing only 6-12% of the full model input, captures most of the information needed for variant effect prediction. Finally, we show that a multi-task model achieves comparable performance to single-task models at a substantially reduced computational cost.

items.title: APH-1A and CDK5 Expression Correlates with Tau Hyperphosphorylation and Its Attenuation by Brahmi and Donep-M in STZ induced Alzheimer’s Disease Model
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressively characterized neurodegenerative condition marked by molecular instability, neuronal dysfunction and abnormal tau buildup. Identification of disease-associated molecular signatures that can be experimentally validated in neuronal models may provide biologically relevant biomarkers and targets for therapeutic intervention. Here, we employed an integrated transcriptomic and cellular approach to identify and validate biomarkers associated with AD pathology. Differential transcriptomic analysis of (AD versus control) samples was used to prioritize candidate genes, followed by experimental validation in a streptozotocin (STZ) induced SH-SY5Y cells. Among the selected genes, anterior pharynx defective 1A (APH-1A) and cyclin dependent kinase (CDK5) were experimentally validated and further correlated to tau pathology by quantifying phosphorylation of tau at serine 396 (p-Tau Ser396) using confocal fluorescence microscopy. Complementary atomic force microscopy (AFM) was employed to characterize STZ-associated cellular morphological alterations. STZ exposure induced an AD-like neuronal phenotype characterized by associated cellular structural abnormalities. Importantly, co-treatment with (Brahmi) attenuated STZ-associated tau Ser396 phosphorylation and improved the cellular phenotype. The effects of Brahmi were further compared with those of established anti-Alzheimer’s drugs, Donep-M (Donepezil and Memantine) together, which similarly reduced p-Tau Ser396-associated alterations. The concordance between molecular biomarker validation and imaging-based phenotypic responses warrants further investigation of underlying molecular mechanisms. Collectively, our findings establish a transcriptome-to-cellular validation framework in which APH-1A and CDK5 represent experimentally supported AD-associated biomarkers. This integrated strategy provides a foundation for connecting human AD molecular signatures with measurable neuronal phenotypes and evaluating potential therapeutic interventions.

items.title: Computational alternative to cardiac biopsy in multiple myeloma: utilizing the shape of routine laboratory data for the classification of AL cardiac amyloidosis
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Patients with multiple myeloma (MM) are at increased risk for light chain cardiac amyloidosis (CA) due to high circulating levels of light chains. ALCA is a clinical diagnosis based on biopsy, cardiac imaging findings of restrictive cardiomyopathy, and serum monoclonal proteins. To overcome these challenges, we have developed machine learning models that accurately predict ALCA status while identifying key diagnostic features based on routine laboratory measurements and using limited data. Methods: Utilizing electronic medical data (EMR) data, we built support vector machine models (SVMs) using the MISTIC framework. Data including diagnosis history, treatment, and laboratory values for patients with MM or monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance (MGUS) were collected as a retrospective cohort study at Moffit Cancer Center and Research Institute between 2014 and 2019. To utilize the wealth of information in longitudinal EMR data, we fit regression models to the EMR data and used the parameters and characteristics of the fits as features for our SVMs. We tested three different sets of features: descriptive statistics alone, parameters and characteristics of fit only, and both the descriptive statistics and parameters of fit (DescFits). A classifier using raw data at a timepoint proximal to the date of ALCA diagnostic imaging (EchoAdj), as well as analogous random forest and XGBoost models were used for comparison. Findings: SVM classifiers trained on the DescFits feature set (AUC= 1.0) outperformed blind model predictions of the EchoAdj model (AUC = 0.36) and other conventional machine learning approaches in identifying which patients were diagnosed with ALCA. The DescFits model selected features describing the temporal relationship of physiologic parameters including hematologic state, and cardiac and renal function. Interpretation: We demonstrated that the MISTIC SVM framework and the shape of EMR data can aid in identifying patients with cardiac amyloidosis without cardiac biopsy or imaging.

items.title: oidyPeaks: R package for automated flow cytometry cell cycle analysis and visualization in fungal microbes
items.abstract_or_text: Karyotypic variation in fungal populations from ecological, clinical, and industrial environments and is also a hallmark of many cancers. The evolutionary dynamics of karyotypic vriants (i.e., changes in the number of chromosomes, either as complete sets or single chromosomes) are the same as any de novo mutation. To quantify karyotypic subpopulations within evolving populations, an unbiased computational method is required to identify subpopulations and quantify their abundance. Flow cytometry is the standard method to measure the genome size from large populations of individual cells. Cell populations typically include cells in all stages of the cell cycle (G0/G1 before DNA replication, S phase during replication, and G2/M after DNA replication but before cell division). Existing mathematical models can be fit to genome-size distributions to determine the base ploidy of a population, but existing algorithms assume a single base ploidy. Mixed-karyotype populations therefore require manual gating to subdivide the flow cytometry data before analysis, which introduces bias, as it is not always clear where or when gates should be drawn. To overcome this, we developed a new method that identifies and quantifies karyotypic subpopulations from flow cytometry data. The open-source R package ploidyPeaks builds on existing Bioconductor tools to import and manipulate standard .fcs flow cytometry files. Using reference populations of known ploidy, we established thresholds to distinguish single-genome size populations and identify candidate mixed-karyotype samples. We then developed a peak-detection algorithm to identify G0/G1 and G2/M peaks, resolve karyotypic subpopulations within mixed populations, and apply nonlinear least-squares fitting of the Dean-Jett-Fox cell-cycle model to each subpopulation, providing a confidence measure for model fit. Compared with existing methods, our approach quantifies genome size in mixed-karyotype populations without manual intervention while providing an objective measure of model fit. We demonstrate the utility of this method on 240 replicate populations initiated from 20 Candida albicans genetic backgrounds evolving for 100 generations to the antifungal drug fluconazole.

items.title: Beyond Billing Codes: An Agentic Large Language Model Pipeline for Extracting Glaucoma Procedural Data from Free-Text Clinical Notes
items.abstract_or_text: Purpose: To evaluate the accuracy of a large language model (LLM)-based agentic workflow to extract procedural data from free-text glaucoma clinical notes in the electronic health record (EHR). Design: Cross-sectional. Subjects: 1,250 subjects in the Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Repository. Methods: Randomly sampled clinical notes from glaucoma encounters dated 2014 to 2024 were labeled by two glaucoma specialists (with an adjudicator as needed) for prior glaucoma-related procedures (name, date, details) and recommended future procedures (name, details). Notes were split into development (10%), validation (10%), and test (80%) sets. Five LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.1, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) were accessed in Microsoft Foundry through HIPAA-compliant containers. The extraction pipeline comprised a three-step agentic workflow (extraction, validation, and conditional revision) followed by text standardization. Detection of procedure data was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Among positive cases, performance was evaluated using exact-match accuracy and Jaccard Index (JI). Prior procedure labels were also compared with EHR glaucoma-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. Main Outcome Measures: Accuracy, exact-match accuracy, JI. Results: A total of 1,984 (992 notes * 2 eyes) labels were evaluated for each task in the test set. Prior and future procedures were identified in 1,057 (53.3%) and 152 (7.7%) eyes, respectively. Accuracy ranged from 0.965 (Grok) to 0.996 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.969 (DeepSeek, Qwen)-0.978 (Claude) for future procedures. Among positive cases, exact-match accuracy ranged from 0.681 (Grok) to 0.890 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.704 (Grok)-0.849 (Claude) for future procedures; JI ranged from 0.827 (Grok) to 0.956 (Claude) and 0.734 (Grok) to 0.883 (Claude), respectively. Among all 1,760 prior procedures present in adjudicated labels, only 441 (25.1%) were captured by CPT-coded EHR data. Conclusions: A secure agentic LLM pipeline accurately extracted glaucoma procedural data from clinical notes, recovering data largely absent from structured EHR fields. Claude performed best across both tasks. Limited agreement between labels and CPT codes likely reflects procedures performed at outside institutions and the limited granularity of CPT coding. This approach may support a scalable, comprehensive characterization of procedure burden among glaucoma patients for research and clinical applications.

items.title: QuantCell: machine learning based cell annotation integrating qualitative and quantitative imaging profiles
items.abstract_or_text: Recent advances in spatial omics enable high-resolution, multiplexed imaging of RNA and protein expression, but cell annotation remains challenging, particularly in complex tissues with numerous markers or rare cell types. Here, we present QuantCell, a machine learning framework that leverages quantitative imaging data to improve annotation derived from qualitative profiles. QuantCell evaluates multiple models and applies a user-defined false discovery rate to ensure high-confidence annotation. Using PhenoCycler imaging of mouse bone marrow, QuantCell increased annotated cells from 33.1% to 90.2% at 5% FDR, achieving 96.5% accuracy. QuantCell supports diverse imaging platforms and robustly detects rare cell populations.

items.title: Harness engineering enables a multi-agent LLM system to generate cross-domain hypotheses beyond single-investigator reach
items.abstract_or_text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate scientific hypotheses, and a more capable model is widely assumed to drive output quality. We tested this with a biology-focused multi-agent system coupling an LLM to five Model Context Protocol servers exposing 66 external tools. Upgrading the Synthesizer and Critic from Claude Sonnet 4.6 to Opus 4.8 initially appeared to improve quality, count, and reliability. Under a fully matched harness (identical prompts, schema, hypothesis count, and queries), the differences vanished: scores were indistinguishable on an iPSC-reprogramming task and favoured Sonnet 4.6 on a CHO cell-line-engineering task (18.4 vs 17.4; Welch t = 2.89, p < 0.05). The dominant, controllable driver of quality is therefore the prompting harness, not the model tier. We then introduce the ABCD-Stack (contract-gated prompting, diversity-first generation, adversarial refinement, and cross-family evaluation), which builds these properties in as architecture and shifts outputs toward explicitly falsifiable, causally framed hypotheses beyond the reach of a single-domain investigator. The hypotheses are falsifiable by construction but not yet experimentally validated.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Tools for Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Classification
items.abstract_or_text: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the common mental disorders affecting children and is often diagnosed with an important delay. This neurodevelopmental disorder is usually identified by symptoms such as a deficit in attention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness. There are clinical and data-oriented methods for ADHD diagnosis. Recently, artificial intelligence techniques for ADHD diagnosis have been taken into consideration. In this article, we have reviewed state-of-the-art deep learning and classical machine learning networks using a wide range of neuroimaging, neurosignal and related data, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), questionnaires, genome data, mo-tion data, performance tests and game simulation. In addition, we identified common validation methods and analyzed them. As an important aspect for clinicians, the brain regions of ADHD patients identified as discriminative by existing machine learning-based studies are investigated. In the end, we identify exiting research gaps, notably the lack of publicly available large-scale multimodal datasets, non-interpretability and inexplicability of many algorithms and the use of architectures that are unable to efficiently model the spatiotemporal features of the brain. Ultimately, we hope that researchers will implement explainable machine learning-based studies that use several neuroimaging modalities to aid clinicians in supporting their decisions for diagnosis, prognosis and for treatment planning.

items.title: Aligning Medical Vision Language Models at the Capability Boundary with Entropy Adaptive Rubric Grounding
items.abstract_or_text: Medical diagnostic reasoning requires verifiable links between visual evidence and clinical knowledge, yet current medical vision language models are aligned with objectives that reward the wrong behavior. Uniform supervised fine tuning lets easy cases dominate updates while clinically critical boundary cases saturate prematurely. Sparse rewards based only on final-answer correctness cannot assess anatomical grounding or clinical logic, inviting reward hacking through answer shortcuts. We propose MedCBR, a two-stage alignment framework coupling boundary-aware preference optimization with rubric-grounded reinforcement learning. First, we construct counterfactual boundary preferences at the model's capability frontier using empirical pass rates and preference pairs that share reasoning prefixes but diverge at decisive diagnostic branches. Difficulty Weighted Boundary Preference Optimization (DBPO) concentrates learning on this calibrated boundary region. Second, we distill reusable clinical rubrics from boundary trajectories and activate them according to prediction entropy. Entropy Gated Grounded Policy Optimization (EGPO) rewards answer correctness, anatomical grounding, and reasoning fidelity while suppressing rubric noise on reliable samples. A reference policy anchored to the boundary-aligned model couples population-level boundary priors with instance-level uncertainty, making diagnostic reasoning more accurate and clinically grounded. Experiments on six medical benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong general, specialized, and reinforcement learning baselines, reaching 61.2% average accuracy with the largest gains on challenging differential diagnosis tasks. Ablations show super-additive gains: combining the two stages exceeds the sum of their individual improvements.

items.title: Integrating stool chemistry measurements with metagenomics in adults reveals distinct gut health profiles
items.abstract_or_text: Stool chemistry metrics, including calprotectin, lactoferrin, and secretory IgA, are used to assess gut inflammation in clinical or research settings. However, these measures in isolation provide a limited view of gut physiology and lack microbial context. Shotgun metagenomics offers a comprehensive assessment of the gut microbiome's taxonomic composition and functional potential, yet its integration with stool chemistry metrics remains underexplored. We analyzed 877 adult stool samples with paired shotgun metagenomic sequencing and chemistry measurements to integrate the microbiome with 12 stool chemistry metrics. Calprotectin, lactoferrin, and secretory IgA were associated with shifts in microbiome composition (beta diversity), while deviations from typical levels of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including butyrate, were associated with both changes in alpha diversity and microbiome composition. Network analysis revealed two distinct microbial neighborhoods: one associated with higher butyrate and lower calprotectin and lactoferrin and another associated with lower butyrate and higher calprotectin and lactoferrin. Machine learning models trained on taxonomic and functional data showed modest discrimination of stool chemistry states, performing best for SCFA deficiency and less well for host-derived inflammatory metrics. Together, these findings systematically characterize microbiome-stool chemistry relationships across a large paired dataset, providing a framework for interpreting stool chemistry metrics in the context of shotgun metagenomic profiles.

items.title: Agentic Discovery Transfer Enables Cross-Cancer Discovery at Scale
items.abstract_or_text: Cancer research generates tens of thousands of studies each year, yet whether a published finding holds in another cancer type or patient population is rarely tested, because doing so is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We define this task as discovery transfer and present SMART, a multi-agent large language model framework for discovery transfer in single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies. Given a source manuscript and a target scRNA-seq dataset, SMART extracts major clinical and mechanistic findings, generates and executes analyses for the testable findings, and reports which findings transfer and suggests follow-up. Applied to 121 studies across six cancer types, SMART identified findings that transfer across cancers, including a lung cancer prognostic signature that we confirmed to be associated with survival in liver cancer, pancreatic cancer and pleural mesothelioma. SMART also generated new mechanistic hypotheses, demonstrating how agentic discovery transfer can extend published findings beyond their original setting.

items.title: Myogenic and neural transcriptional circuitry determines PAX3::FOXO1 driven initiation of rhabdomyosarcoma
items.abstract_or_text: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS) is largely characterized by the PAX3::FOXO1 (P3F) fusion oncoprotein, yet the mechanisms by which P3F initiates tumorigenesis and cell identity remain incompletely understood. Here, we describe a doxycycline inducible, degradable PAX3::FOXO1 iPSC derived ARMS model (ddP3F) to interrogate the temporal requirements of P3F for ARMS cell identity and proliferation. We show that, while P3F is essential for initiating ARMS transformation from precursor cells, continued expression of P3F is not required for maintaining proliferation, viability, or RMS associated transcriptional programs. Integration of CUT&RUN, bulk RNA seq, and 10X multiome profiling during endothelial-directed differentiation revealed that P3F rapidly pioneers a novel enhancer landscape within two days of expression, activating transcriptional circuits anchored by both specific myogenic and neural transcription factors (TFs), including MYOD1, PRDM12, and POU4F1 (BRN3A). Our single-cell analysis shows that these TFs are specifically co-expressed with P3F from the earliest stages of transformation. Knockout of MYOD1 or POU4F1 impairs ARMS identity acquisition without preventing transformation, whereas PRDM12 loss enhances P3F expression programs and myogenic differentiation. Together, these findings underscore a previously unappreciated interplay between myogenic and neural transcriptional programs during ARMS initiation. Furthermore, these data demonstrate that P3F establishes a stable oncogenic state that persists even after removal, thus providing a framework for evaluating P3F dependent and P3F independent therapeutic vulnerabilities.

items.title: Photograph-Based Skeletal Malocclusion Screening with Geometric Machine Learning: External Validation Across Turkish and Non-European Cohorts
items.abstract_or_text: A photograph based screening classifier for skeletal malocclusion maps 100 engineered geometric feature vectors, derived from a side-profile smartphone photograph, to orthodontic class labels, enabling non-invasive triage without radiographic imaging. This study reports external validation across two independent cohorts that contributed no cases to training. Two binary tasks were evaluated; Class III against non-Class III, and Class I against Class II; each with its own development set and model, applied without modification at the default threshold. One external cohort was Turkish, drawn from an institution not represented in the development set; the other was a non-European cohort from a Belgian private orthodontic clinic. Sensitivity, specificity and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were pre-specified as primary outcome measures, since none depends on outcome prevalence. In the Class III task, sensitivity was similar across all three evaluation sets (0.801, 0.836, 0.848; all adjusted p>0.7), while specificity fell from 0.766 in the Turkish external cohort to 0.697 in the non-European cohort. AUC was 0.902 and 0.835 respectively (difference 0.066; p=0.029). In the Class I and Class II task the corresponding values were 0.875 and 0.723 (difference 0.152; p<0.001). A subgroup analysis showed lower sensitivity in children than adults across both cohorts (0.71 to 0.80 versus 0.89 to 0.90). AUC was lower in the non-European cohort for all three models in both tasks. The observed performance differences are consistent with a population-specific generalizability effect rather than model-specific failure and support mandatory external validation on target populations before clinical deployment.

items.title: The Alzheimer's disease-associated rs28834970 variant in PTK2B impairs electrical activity and regulates Tau phosphorylation and APP processing in human neuronal cultures
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Genome-wide association studies have identified the PTK2B gene, which encodes Proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (PYK2), as a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, its role in AD aetiology remains to be understood, as a complex contribution to amyloid {beta} (A{beta}) toxicity, tauopathy and neuronal dysfunction is suggested by contradictory evidence. Determining how the causal variant among AD-associated PTK2B variants impairs PYK2 function to trigger AD hallmarks could bring clarification. Methods: We combined in silico prediction tools with luciferase reporter assays in neuroblastoma cells to prioritize potential AD-associated PTK2B functional variants. We generated isogenic KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) carrying the most relevant functional variant using CRISPR-Cas9 and differentiated them into human neuronal cultures (hNCs). We assessed PYK2 expression via immunoblotting, performed transcriptomic profiling using RNA-sequencing, analyzed neuronal network activity via multielectrode array (MEA) recordings, quantified synaptic density through immunocytochemistry in microfluidic devices, and assessed Tau phosphorylation and amyloid-precursor protein (APP) metabolism. Results: The rs28834970 regulatory variant was identified as the most functionally relevant in our model, with the C risk allele promoting transcription factor C/EBP{beta} binding within a cis-regulatory element. In hNCs, the homozygous rs28834970 CC genotype reduced total PYK2 levels by more than 80%, while increasing the proportion of phosphorylated (activated) PYK2. Transcriptomic analysis revealed 724 downregulated and 113 upregulated gene sets, with altered expression of genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, cytoplasmic translation and neurotransmitter secretion. MEA recordings showed reduced network recruitment and altered burst organization. Immunocytochemistry in microfluidic devices consistently revealed that rs28834970 impacts dendritic development and postsynaptic maturation. The risk genotype significantly elevated Tau phosphorylation at pathological sites (Thr181, Thr217, Thr231, Ser202-Thr205, Ser396-Ser404), and enhanced APP processing, resulting in decreased levels of APP and CTF but increased levels of sAPP, sAPP{beta} and A{beta}. Conclusion: The rs28834970 C risk allele mechanistically links AD susceptibility to downregulation of PTK2B/PYK2 expression and to the increase in Tau pathology and A{beta} levels while compromising synaptic structure and function.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Early Prediction of Neural Microelectrode Lifetime Under Accelerated Aging Conditions
items.abstract_or_text: Objective. Chronically implantable medical devices may require functional lifetimes of decades in order to reduce or eliminate the need for their explantation and replacement, which may involve invasive and sometimes risky surgery. However, when devices become exceptionally long-lived, preclinical studies validating their lifetimes become difficult to execute within reasonable timeframes even when accelerated life testing methods are employed. Computational methods capable of accurately and reliably predicting microelectrode lifetime from early-life data could therefore considerably expedite the development of long-lived implantable devices. Approach. Here, inspired by similar studies predicting functional lifetimes of lithium-ion battery cells from early-life data, we developed a machine learning model based on Elastic Net regression and early-life feature engineering to predict impedance-defined microelectrode lifetimes under accelerated aging conditions and evaluated its predictive performance. We also provide a dataset of electrochemical measurements from aging microelectrodes for public use. Main results. Using measurements collected through Day 5, the 10-feature Elastic Net model achieved a root mean squared error of 3.71 accelerated-aging days and a mean absolute percentage error of 13.90% under device-level validation. In an independent fabrication batch, covariance alignment and calibration using five labeled channels from one device in each target group reduced mean absolute percentage errors from 38.1% to 22.5% for Small electrodes and from 56.6% to 18.2% for Medium electrodes. Significance. These results highlight the potential of machine learning-based approaches to accurately predict neural microelectrode lifetimes from early-life data. Such methods may inform the design of future accelerated life studies, providing meaningful longevity estimates from shorter testing periods and potentially accelerating the development of long-lived implantable devices for clinical use.

items.title: Deep Learning Based Cell Segmentation of 3D Confocal Images of Wood for Enzymatic Hydrolysis Applications
items.abstract_or_text: Plant cell walls are an abundant renewable resource for biobased products, but their recalcitrance limits enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency. Cell and tissue morphological parameters provide reliable biomarkers for predicting enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency. Accurate cell segmentation in 3D microscopy images is essential for quantifying these parameters. Although deep learning has achieved high performance in biological image segmentation, confocal microscopy's limited penetration depth leaves elongated wood cells partially imaged, creating open-ended structures that challenge existing segmentation methods. Based on an artificial longitudinal domain restriction, an adapted framework is presented here for the training of a 3D U-net model for the cell segmentation of wood images. Quantitative evaluation on a dedicated benchmark dataset identified a model configuration that reduced segmentation errors and produced more robust predictions during early enzymatic hydrolysis. These results support the use of the framework to quantify morphological parameters relevant to assessing and predicting biomass conversion efficiency.

items.title: Discipline of Language Models Reviewing Data Extracted From Genomic Reports Under Full and Partial Evidence: Plausibility Bias, Erasure, and the Effect of a Keep Rule
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are used as reviewers of tables extracted by an earlier step of a pipeline. In this role, the model must keep correct values even when they look wrong, correct errors, and, when it cannot verify a value, flag it instead of erasing it. We found no studies that measure these three behaviours separately. Methods. Thirteen models from seven developers reviewed tables of 33 to 40 cells extracted from three synthetic clinical exome reports. Each report has an identical twin in which the correct target value is counterintuitive (implausible twin) or common (plausible twin), plus planted plausible and implausible errors. The models received the full report or an excerpt without the sections that prove the counterintuitive values, with a statement that the table had been prepared from the full report. Four instructions (neutral, true alert, mandatory citation, keep rule) and three levels of reasoning effort were compared. A mechanical grader classified each cell as kept, kept and flagged, erased, flipped, corrected, or not corrected. A total of 3,019 responses were analysed. Results. In the 12 models with a reasoning parameter, correct counterintuitive values were flipped in 1 of 970 cells (0.1%; 95% CI 0.02% to 0.58%). Llama 4 Maverick, without reasoning, flipped 8 of 45 in the full report and 7 of 36 in the excerpt, always “female” to “male” in a 46,XY patient with androgen insensitivity. Without the proof in the excerpt, the models diverged: Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon kept almost everything and flagged it; GPT-6.1 Sol and Sol Pro erased 27 of 36 cells in each twin and changed on average 5.0 non-target cells per response. Erasure was equal in the two twins, which indicates a reaction to the literal absence of the text, not to plausibility. A keep sentence brought erasure to zero in 10 of the 13 models; raising reasoning effort cost 1.1 to 21.5 times more tokens and reduced erasure in only three models. Conclusions. In models with reasoning, the risk is not the flipping of atypical values but the erasure of correct values under partial evidence. This behaviour is a default of some models and disappears with an explicit keep instruction.

items.title: Effects of Nano-Hydroxyapatite-Coated Platelet-Rich Fibrin on In Vitro Wound Healing of Gingiva-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Objectives: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) contains bioactive mediators that may support cellular events involved in wound healing. This study compared the effects of conditioned media derived from leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF), nano-hydroxyapatite-modified PRF (HA-PRF), and titanium-prepared PRF (T-PRF) on gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) wound closure using an in vitro scratch assay. Materials and Methods : GMSCs were isolated from gingival tissue obtained from a healthy donor and characterized before experimental use. L-PRF, HA-PRF, and T-PRF membranes were prepared under identical centrifugation conditions, and conditioned media were collected after 1 or 3 days of incubation. GMSCs were seeded in 24-well plates, serum-starved, and subjected to a linear scratch. Following exposure to the respective conditioned media, residual wound areas were evaluated at 0, 6, 12, 24, 30, and 36 h. Comparisons among the control, L-PRF, HA-PRF, and T-PRF groups were performed at each observation time using one-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey’s post hoc test where appropriate. Results : For 1-day conditioned media, no significant differences among groups were observed at 6, 12, or 24 h (all p > 0.05), whereas a significant between-group difference was detected at 30 h (p = 0.005), when complete wound closure had occurred in the L-PRF and HA-PRF groups. For 3-day conditioned media, no significant between-group difference was observed at 6 h (p = 0.209), whereas a significant difference emerged at 12 h (p Conclusions : PRF-conditioned media supported GMSC wound closure, with HA-PRF showing the most favorable early response, particularly with conditioned medium collected after 3 days. These findings suggest that nano-hydroxyapatite modification may enhance the early biological activity of PRF; however, further mechanistic and in vivo studies are required. Clinical Relevance : Nano-hydroxyapatite modification of PRF may enhance early GMSC-mediated wound closure and may represent a promising approach for improving the regenerative potential of PRF in oral and periodontal wound healing.

items.title: Mitochondrial genome editing reveals the impact of complex I heteroplasmic variants on human neurogenesis
items.abstract_or_text: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variants, whether maternally inherited or acquired somatically during aging, can be particularly detrimental to cells that rely on mitochondrial metabolism such as neurons. The functional consequences of mtDNA variants are thought to depend on their heteroplasmy, defined as the proportion of mtDNA molecules carrying that variant. However, investigating the specific effects of heteroplasmic mtDNA variants on human neuronal function has been challenging. Studies using patient-derived cells cannot conclusively attribute observed phenotypes to a single mtDNA variant, while conventional genome editing approaches are not applicable to mtDNA. Here, we use DddA-derived cytosine base editor (DdCBE) to introduce pathogenic heteroplasmic mtDNA variants into Neurogenin 2 (NGN2)-inducible human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). We focus on two variants in the genes MT-ND1 and MT-ND5 belonging to complex I (CI), the largest component of the mitochondrial respiratory chain and a frequent contributor to human disease, including the incurable neurodevelopmental disorder Leigh syndrome. mtDNA-edited iPSC lines exhibit low off-target editing and maintain similar heteroplasmy following subclonal isolation and differentiation into NGN2-induced neurons (iNs). Although the CI variants do not substantially affect mitochondrial energy metabolism in undifferentiated iPSCs, they reduce mitochondrial membrane potential in iNs where they drive a transcriptional reprogramming indicative of impaired neuronal commitment. These findings suggest that heteroplasmic CI variants are sufficient to disrupt neural fate specification even at relatively low heteroplasmy. More broadly, mtDNA editing in human iPSCs provides a powerful platform to investigate how mitochondrial fitness and heteroplasmy influence development and disease.

items.title: COG5-mediated Golgi organization coordinates neural progenitor fate during human brain development
items.abstract_or_text: Apical radial glial cells (aRGs) are highly polarized epithelial cells that drive human cortical development through tightly regulated lineage progression. A distinctive feature of aRGs is their non-canonical Golgi organization, raising the possibility that specialized intracellular trafficking and secretory processes contribute to progenitor behaviour. However, how Golgi architecture contributes to human corticogenesis remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this question in the context of COG5 deficiency, a rare congenital disorder of glycosylation associated with neurodevelopmental defects, using patient-derived fibroblasts and brain organoids, N-glycomics, glycolipidomics, and single-cell transcriptomics. We show that COG5 deficiency disrupts Golgi organization and impairs Golgi-to-ER retrograde trafficking. At the neurodevelopmental level, COG5-deficient organoids display altered ventricular organization and reduced basal progenitor abundance. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals rewired developmental trajectories characterized by premature differentiation from apical progenitors with activation of neuronal pathways. Despite the absence of major abnormalities in plasma glycoproteins glycosylation, glycolipidomic analysis identified marked defects in glycosphingolipid maturation within patient-derived brain organoids, indicating selective impairment of neural lipid glycosylation. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed dysregulation of developmental pathways, including reduced Notch signalling and altered localization of both cleaved Notch1 and the Golgi-associated protein ACBD3. Consistent with impaired progenitor maintenance, COG5-deficient organoids displayed altered cleavage plane orientation in apical progenitors. Together, our findings suggest a link between Golgi organization, intracellular trafficking, membrane glycosylation, and lineage progression in human neural progenitors, identifying Golgi architecture as an important regulator of apical radial glial cell biology and cortical development.

items.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
items.abstract_or_text: RNA language models have achieved strong performance across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by hierarchical structure, making structural information important for pre-training. Existing approaches often depend on noisy annotations or task-specific objectives that can limit generalizability. Here we present structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million RNA sequence--structure pairs by integrating base-pairing interactions into masked language modelling through a pair-matching operation. We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks among the leading models in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold3 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

items.title: DiaBench: A Benchmarking Framework to Evaluate the Performance of LLMs in T2D Patient Education
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods: We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question-and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-51, Gemini-2.5-Flash2, Cohere Command3, Llama-44, DeepSeek-R15, Perplexity Sonar6, Mistral-Large-2.07) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results: (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy (≥95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models (≥95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions: DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

items.title: Biologically grounded locality priors close the data gap for vision transformers in neural prediction
items.abstract_or_text: For datasets with thousands of neurons and images, vision transformers have proven successful at predicting neural responses to stimuli. However, they are expected to underperform in low-data regimes, where CNNs and Gaussian processes are considered more effective. We ask whether transformers can be made competitive for small-scale neural prediction, and show that underperformance in this regime can be overturned with the right inductive bias. We equip a vision transformer with a differentiable per-neuron circular crop in feature space. The crop is centered on each neuron's receptive field, with a radius selected per neuron, so the model only sees the small image region that drives that neuron instead of the whole image. This makes the cost of attention scale with the size of the receptive field rather than with the size of the image. A single transformer stack is shared across all neurons: each neuron's specificity resides in the crop, not in the architecture. We call this model circular receptive-field vision transformer (CiRF-ViT). We evaluate it on small multi-electrode-array recordings of mouse and salamander retinas: a mouse preparation of 41 ganglion cells and two salamander preparations totaling 49 ganglion cells, each with only a few thousand stimulus-response pairs, two orders of magnitude below the scale at which transformers are typically trained. Against CNN and Gaussian-process baselines, CiRF-ViT reaches the highest mean explained variance on both datasets (0.94 on mouse, 0.95 on salamander). Probed with the local spike-triggered average (LSTA), a zero-shot test of context-dependent, nonlinear stimulus sensitivity, CiRF-ViT reproduces the qualitative polarity inversion that a linear model cannot capture by construction. A biologically grounded, per-neuron locality prior is therefore enough to make transformers competitive for neural prediction well below their usual data scale, while matching the reference models on an established functional signature of the retina's nonlinear computation.

items.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
items.abstract_or_text: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis-regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we quantify the frequency with which pairs of positions are simultaneously accessible on individual molecules. Then, we train ChAI-Net, a neural network that predicts these locus-specific chromatin co-accessibility maps from the underlying DNA sequence. Through model interpretation and in silico experiments, we show that ChAI-Net learns unique combinations of sequence motifs underlying co-accessibility within enhancers, promoters, and CTCF-bound sites. Many of these motifs are missed when modeling average accessibility, suggesting a specific role in coordinated binding. ChAI-Net's regulatory grammar also highlights the importance of TF motif orientation, spacing, positioning, and co-occurrence in driving co-accessibility. Thus, our framework for extracting regulatory rules from footprinting data expands understanding of TF cooperativity, while laying the groundwork to elucidate how these rules vary across cellular contexts as single-molecule genomics is deployed at scale.

items.title: Parameters for stable Notch-independent Her6 oscillations across a frequency spectrum in neural stem cell populations
items.abstract_or_text: Neural proliferation zones drive strong and persistent growth of the developing vertebrate brain. How Notch signaling and HES/Her transcription factors in vivo maintain stable neural stem cell (NSC) populations during brain growth is not well understood. Genetic evidence revealed Her6, a Notch-independent homolog of mammalian HES1, to be essential for maintenance of zebrafish NSCs. We recombined mNeonGreen into the her6 locus and analyzed temporal Her6-mNG fluorescence profiles in vivo. Her6 is expressed dynamically in all NSCs, with a majority revealing stable oscillation, albeit from cell to cell across a wide frequency range. Her6 oscillates cell-autonomously, unaffected by inhibition of Notch, and is robustly reinitiated after experimental perturbations. Mathematical modelling predicts, and we indeed find in vivo, that Her6 oscillations prevail only when both transcript and protein degradation rate constants are equal. These intrinsic control parameters may have evolved for the Her6 oscillator to contribute to robust maintenance of NSCs.

items.title: CD4 T cell surface architecture is associated with response to anti-PD-1 therapy in non-small cell lung cancer
items.abstract_or_text: Anti-PD-1 therapy has substantially improved outcomes for patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but clinical responses remain highly heterogeneous and are difficult to predict. Current immune profiling approaches primarily characterize immune cell composition and protein abundance, whereas the spatial organization of proteins at the cell surface has remained largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate for the first time that cell surface protein organization is associated with clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibition therapy. Using the Proximity Network Assay (PNA), we simultaneously quantified cell frequencies, protein abundance, and protein organization in pretreatment peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 62 patients with advanced NSCLC treated with anti-PD-1 agents. While most cell populations were unchanged between responders and non-responders, pronounced response-associated alterations were identified within the CD4 T-cell compartment. Responders exhibited elevated expression of adhesion-associated proteins, and remodeling of a CD5-containing membrane domain. Increased colocalization within this domain was associated with poor clinical outcome and reduced survival. Machine learning analysis further identified CD4 T cell features as the strongest predictors of treatment response and demonstrated that protein organization provided greater predictive power than protein abundance alone. Together, these findings identify cell surface protein organization as a previously unexplored source of biomarkers and highlight its potential to improve immune profiling and biomarker discovery in cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Advancing Clinical Genomic Analysis with a Skill-Centred Agent
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical genomic analysis requires experts to integrate evolving guidelines, databases, and computational evidence. As sequencing has become increasingly accessible, this complex and labor-intensive process has become a major bottleneck to the timely use of genomic information in clinical decision-making. To fill this gap, we developed ClinGeX, a large-language-model agent that composes 105 curated executable skills through task-specific retrieval and dependency-aware orchestration. On 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, ClinGeX achieved 71.7\% macro-averaged task-level concordance with expert reference classifications, compared with 45.7\% for the strongest comparator. In a three-condition, counterbalanced human-AI collaboration study, 45 clinical genomic professionals assessed 135 clinically derived cases under routine (no AI assistance), DeepSeek-assisted and ClinGeX-assisted conditions. ClinGeX assistance increased raw case-level concordance across criterion-level variant analysis, genomic interpretation in rare disease and molecular oncology decision-making (51.1\%, 57.8\%, 64.4\% versus 15.6\%, 31.1\%, 20.0\% in comparator conditions) and reduced reported interpretation time in all scenarios. During an exploratory one-month real-world non-interventional assessment, 11 experienced professionals submitted feedback on 96 self-selected analysis episodes and reported frequent conclusion adoption and time savings. These findings support executable domain skills as a promising approach to augment specialist genomic interpretation.

items.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables
items.abstract_or_text: Large language model (LLM) agents for personal health read wearable data and recommend, but do not learn about the individual in a way that can be audited or falsified. We present EpiCoach, an agentic system that treats one athlete, a cross-country mountain biker, as the subject of accountable N-of-1 science. Claims about the athlete live in an evidence-gated hypothesis registry: each must issue a probabilistic prediction about a future session before it occurs, and its belief moves only through computed evidence from a logged statistical fit. Predictions come from a mechanistic digital twin inferred from heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude: a lagged heart-rate response model, a fitness-fatigue model with learned time constants, and a latent technical-descending skill state, measured on discovered trail segments. The agent prescribes the next training week as a constrained experiment maximizing information gain subject to load and safety constraints, around two instrument rides. We evaluate the system two ways over eighteen months of data. A rolling-origin replay benchmark shows the twin beats standard forecasters on heart rate but not segment time, and the agentic loop matches a static model. A live prospective phase runs the weekly cycle: in its first three weeks the ledger sealed 20 predictions, scored 14, the descent forecast calibrated after one correction, the climb forecast pessimistic as the athlete improved, and the safety officer vetoed the agent twice. Every correction is preserved in the registry, a template for auditable, falsifiable personalization in digital health. We release the registry, benchmark and protocol.

items.title: What Makes Medical Examination Items Difficult? Using Large Language Models to Explore Patterns Associated With Empirical Item Difficulty
items.abstract_or_text: Research on medical item difficulty has largely focused on prediction rather than on identifying interpretable patterns associated with empirical difficulty. This study used empirical difficulty labels to guide large language models (LLMs) in inducing difficulty rubrics and examined how rubric guidance affected LLM difficulty judgments. Using training items and their empirical difficulty estimates from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) and the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE), Claude Opus 5 induced separate rubrics for absolute and pairwise difficulty judgment. None of the induced rubrics treated surface features, such as stem length, option count, or images, as major sources of difficulty. Several patterns emerged across both examinations, including cue convergence, misleading cues, and option competition, although their specific forms differed. Retrieval of knowledge that could not be derived from the stem was particularly prominent in the PANCE rubrics, whereas the USMLE rubrics placed greater emphasis on integrating multiple clinical cues. We compared commercial and open-weight LLMs on held-out items under unguided and rubric-guided conditions. Rubric guidance changed how models used the difficulty scale but did not consistently improve performance. In absolute judgments, guidance encouraged broader use of the scale and generally improved coarse-grained agreement, without consistently improving rank ordering. In pairwise comparisons, its effects varied across models and examinations, and judgments became more sensitive to presentation order. These findings suggest that the value of label-guided rubric induction may lie more in generating interpretable, testable hypotheses from empirical difficulty data than in reliably improving difficulty judgments.

items.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
items.abstract_or_text: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient- and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types. To address the bottleneck between gene program identification and interpretation, we developed an AI agent framework built on off-the-shelf large language models (e.g., Gemini 2.5) to interpret gene expression programs at the level of human experts, but at much greater scale and speed. Our agent identified ectopic expression of neuronal marker genes as a unique feature of several fusion-driven sarcomas. This gene expression pattern resulted in tumor-specific co-expression of mixed mesenchymal/neuronal surface markers, providing a plausible therapeutic window to target these tumor types using emerging AND-gated therapeutic strategies, such as bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and bispecific CAR-T cells. As proof of principle, we nominated and validated STEAP1/NPTXR as a Ewing sarcoma candidate cell surface target pair. Together, this work delivers a pan-pediatric solid tumor scRNA-seq atlas, establishes a generalizable and accessible AI-based framework that complements existing single-cell methods by automating interpretation of pan-disease single-cell atlases, and nominates new bispecific ADC/CAR-T targets for catastrophic pediatric cancers.

items.title: Multi-resolution humanness scoring of antibodies via a region-isolated language model
items.abstract_or_text: Antibodies recognized as foreign can elicit anti-drug antibodies that compromise efficacy and safety, making humanness scoring, estimating how human-like a sequence appears, an early, repeated step in antibody development. Widely used scores reduce a variable domain to a single framework-dominated number, leaving the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) grafted during humanization, diversified by generative models weakly supervised and rarely audited. Here we introduce IgScope, a 23-million-parameter antibody language model trained from scratch that scores humanness at chain, IMGT-region, and residue resolution; a region-isolated attention module confines attention to within-region pairs, and chimeric-sequence training supplies region-level supervision. On 2.38 million held-out chains, masking all framework tokens leaves CDR accuracy unchanged, and back-mutated murine residues in human frameworks are detected at 93.4% accuracy. At chain level, IgScope matches the strongest published correlation with clinical anti-drug-antibody incidence (r = 0.567, n = 217) and outperforms a same-protocol recomputation. Region-level scoring exposes what chain-level scoring conceals: antibodies designed de novo by four generative models pass whole-chain humanness (0.966-0.988), while their CDRs score far below natural (P < 1e-30) in every chain class. Quality control turns the same resolution to the mirror-image question: in humanized-mouse platforms, whose domains are human by design, IgScope scores the domain as human and, in HUGO-Nano chimeric VHHs, isolates only the FR2 signal of four camelid hallmark residues deliberately retained to stabilize the VHH. IgScope gives antibody humanization a verified foundation and generative design an audit.

items.title: Probing Genomic Foundation Models with Splice-Variant Perturbations
items.abstract_or_text: As benchmarks saturate, traditional validation methods fail to capture the probabilistic representations of genomic foundation models.
